regression_matrix.title: Invisible content rendering on all destination detail pages
regression_matrix.evidence: 10 of 12 sampled destinations render full content with proper h1/h2/h3 + JSON-LD. Spiti continues to render the homepage fallback (long-known soft-404). Shimla EN regressed today: HTTP 200, correct <title> and OG metadata, but the rendered body is the 'Lost in the mountains / 404' fallback (NEXT_HTTP_ERROR_FALLBACK marker present). Status flipped from NOT_REPRODUCED to PARTIAL because Shimla is a top-12 destination and the same render-vs-data divergence is the BUG-001 family signature.

regression_matrix.title: Only 1 of 20 collections rendering
regression_matrix.evidence: /en/collections lists 91 unique collection links (≥80 bar). 4 of 4 real-slug probes rendered 200 with content; only the 2 probes I made up returned 404 (expected).

regression_matrix.title: 503 Service Unavailable on RSC prefetch
regression_matrix.evidence: GET /en/destination/jaipur with header 'RSC: 1' returned 200, content-type text/x-component, 203176 bytes in 0.796 s. RSC payload begins with 'react.fragment' marker — well-formed.

regression_matrix.title: Empty modal flash between wizard steps
regression_matrix.evidence: /en/plan rendered as a single-step form with 43 chip buttons + 1 slider. 0 dialog/modal elements present on load. No flash observed during chip toggling.

regression_matrix.title: Hindi translation only partially applied
regression_matrix.evidence: Hindi destination titles + h1 + body render in Devanagari (verified across 11 of 12 slugs). However /hi/collections/<slug> titles still keep the English collection name with only the suffix 'संग्रह | NakshIQ' translated (3 of 3 real-slug probes). /hi/destination/<slug>/march title is fully English ('Jaipur in March 2026: ...') — NEW-2026-05-03-002 still active.

regression_matrix.title: Duration field shows '- days' (missing data)
regression_matrix.evidence: Plan page shows 'How many days? 7d' with a 3..30 day slider; default value rendered as '7d', no '- days' string in body.

regression_matrix.title: Map markers vs results count mismatch
regression_matrix.evidence: 3 destination pages inspected via Chrome (Jaipur, Manali, Leh). Each renders exactly 1 .leaflet-container (1512×384 px on Jaipur) but 0 .leaflet-marker-icon and 0 vector marker children. Pages have 6–8 'Places to visit'-class headings, so the data side has rows that should plot. Severity unchanged from prior run.

regression_matrix.title: Duplicate 'NakshIQ' in destination page titles
regression_matrix.evidence: All 24 destination probes (12 slugs × 2 locales) show exactly one 'NakshIQ' suffix per <title>. Shimla-EN's title is correct even though its body is the 404 fallback.

regression_matrix.title: Treks page title contradicts body content count
regression_matrix.evidence: /en/treks renders h1 'Treks & Hikes', 136 trek-card links and body string '136 treks' — counts agree.

regression_matrix.title: Filter bar disappears after Clear Filters
regression_matrix.evidence: After clicking Clear Filters on /en/explore, URL navigates to /en/explore?month=0 and the listing pane keeps showing '0 destinations'. Beyond the original disappearance complaint, today's deeper finding is that the listing pane returns 0 destinations BEFORE clearing too — the explore listing is empty in default state across both Grid and Map views (see NEW-2026-05-04-002).

regression_matrix.title: 930 network requests on single page load
regression_matrix.evidence: Cold load of /en/destination/jaipur measured 66 resource entries in performance.getEntriesByType('resource'); Manali warm-cache load also 66. Far below the 930 figure that triggered the original report.

regression_matrix.title: Multiple GoTrueClient instances warning (Supabase)
regression_matrix.evidence: Console captured during /en/destination/jaipur load showed only Chrome-extension WTP logs; no GoTrueClient/Supabase/Multiple-instances warnings emitted by the page itself.

regression_matrix.title: Heading hierarchy skips H2 entirely
regression_matrix.evidence: Working destination pages have h2 counts ranging 24–38 and h3 counts 26–61. Pages with 0 h2/h3 (Shimla-EN, Spiti) are soft-404 cases, not hierarchy defects.

regression_matrix.title: Card images slow to load (lazy loading too aggressive)
regression_matrix.evidence: On the 3 destination pages inspected interactively (Jaipur, Manali, Leh), the split is consistent: 17–19 imgs marked loading=lazy, 0 imgs marked loading=eager, 28 imgs with no loading attribute. Hero/above-the-fold imagery appears in the no-attribute bucket rather than being explicitly eager — unchanged from 2026-05-03. Status escalated from PARTIAL_UNVERIFIABLE to PARTIAL because the eager-zero pattern is now reproduced across multiple destinations.

new_defects.title: /en/destination/shimla regressed to 404 fallback body (HTTP 200) on a top-12 destination
new_defects.evidence: 3 cache-busted curls all returned the same 75136-byte HTML containing a NEXT_HTTP_ERROR_FALLBACK;404 digest and the rendered body 'Lost in the mountains / 404 / This trail doesn't exist…'. Title, og:title, og:image, hreflang and JSON-LD organization block all resolve correctly. /api/weather?id=shimla and /api/alerts?id=shimla both return real data. /hi/destination/shimla, /en/destination/shimla/march and /en/destination/shimla/may all render the full destination page. Deployment fingerprint dpl_7Xu6wG5Swk2RGd8LkrRxZVJJ1MDq.
new_defects.impact: Shimla is one of the most-trafficked destinations on the site. EN-locale users and search crawlers receive a 404 page for the canonical URL while the underlying data is healthy. High soft-404 risk in GSC and cannibalisation of Shimla rankings if the EN canonical stays broken.
new_defects.recommended_owner: web app (Next.js destination page render) — investigate why ENGLISH locale at the parent /destination/<slug> route falls through to the not-found fallback while month sub-routes and Hindi parent both render normally.
new_defects.reproduction: curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code} %{size_download}\n' https://www.nakshiq.com/en/destination/shimla → 200 75136. grep -c NEXT_HTTP_ERROR_FALLBACK on the body → 1.

new_defects.title: /en/explore returns 0 destinations across Grid view, Map view and all month filters
new_defects.evidence: Default load shows 'Explore — 0 destinations · Filter or browse the map' and '0 destinations found · Showing scores for May'. Clicking Clear Filters navigates to /en/explore?month=0 and still shows 0 destinations. Forcing /en/explore?month=4 shows 0 destinations. Forcing /en/explore?month=4&view=map shows 0 leaflet containers, 0 markers and 0 destination links. Filter chips for State, Month, Difficulty, Kids Friendly, Solo-female all render — only the listing/map pane is empty.
new_defects.impact: One of the two primary destination-discovery surfaces is unusable. Users hitting /en/explore see a dead grid; the Map view also fails to render any leaflet container. Likely cratered click-throughs from /en into destination pages.
new_defects.recommended_owner: web app (explore listing query) — likely either the destinations RSC fetch or the score-by-month filter logic. The destinations exist (sitemap chunk 1 still has 12766 entries; individual destination pages render normally).
new_defects.reproduction: Load https://www.nakshiq.com/en/explore in any browser. Body text 'No destinations match your filters' is shown beneath an empty grid even with no filters active.

new_defects.title: /api/itinerary returns HTTP 500 with empty body on a payload that uses sensible field names
new_defects.evidence: POST /api/itinerary {"destination":"jaipur","days":3,"month":4} → 500, 0 bytes body. The 4 other malformed payloads I tried (different field names — destinations[], slug, duration, start/end) all returned a clean 400 with body {"error":"Missing required fields"}. The one payload that hits the 500 path uses the exact field names a caller would guess from the schema, suggesting the validator is partially attempting to use the payload and crashing in the body of the route rather than the validator.
new_defects.impact: Any client (LLM, sandbox, integration) that POSTs a roughly-correct payload gets a 500 with no error body — uncatchable on the client side. Should at minimum return a structured 400.
new_defects.recommended_owner: web app (itinerary route handler) — wrap whatever throws in this branch and surface a structured error response.

new_defects.title: Soft-404 on /destination/<bad-slug> persists in BOTH locales — 9th consecutive day
new_defects.evidence: GET /en/destination/this-does-not-exist-xyz → 200 + NEXT_HTTP_ERROR_FALLBACK body. GET /hi/destination/this-does-not-exist-xyz → 200 + NEXT_HTTP_ERROR_FALLBACK body. Same canary URL has been used since 2026-04-26 and has returned 200 every day. The matrix says this should be 404.
new_defects.impact: Crawlers index junk slugs; indexNow / GSC report soft-404 on every nonsense slug crawlers find. Skill explicitly calls this out as a current defect. Continues to cap content-quality signal in GSC.
new_defects.recommended_owner: web app (destination [slug] route handler) — return notFound() / 404 when the destination row is missing instead of falling through to the 200 fallback shell.

new_defects.title: Hindi month sub-route /hi/destination/<slug>/<month> still ships an English-only <title>
new_defects.evidence: /hi/destination/jaipur/march → <title>Jaipur in March 2026: Great time (15–30°C) | NakshIQ</title>. /hi/destination/shimla/march → <title>Shimla in March 2026: Great time (8–18°C) | NakshIQ</title>. Two Hindi sample routes today, both English titles. Body content is also English on these routes.
new_defects.impact: Hindi-locale month pages send an English signal to Google, and the Hindi audience sees English copy on the month-specific landing page even though the parent /hi/destination/<slug> page is fully translated.
new_defects.recommended_owner: web app (month sub-route page metadata + body i18n).

new_defects.title: Numeric month sub-routes /destination/<slug>/<1-12> still soft-404 — llms.txt contract still broken
new_defects.evidence: /en/destination/jaipur/3, /en/destination/shimla/3, /en/destination/manali/3, /hi/destination/jaipur/3, /hi/destination/shimla/3 — all return 200 with the homepage <title> and a NEXT_HTTP_ERROR_FALLBACK body. llms.txt advertises numeric month sub-routes as a stable contract.
new_defects.impact: Any LLM agent that follows the llms.txt instructions to fetch /destination/<slug>/<1-12> gets a homepage soft-404 instead of the destination's monthly card. Breaks the documented bot-friendly contract.
new_defects.recommended_owner: web app — either route /<slug>/<1-12> through the same handler as /<slug>/<name> or update llms.txt to drop the numeric form.
new_defects.reproduction: curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' https://www.nakshiq.com/en/destination/jaipur/3 → 200; grep NEXT_HTTP_ERROR_FALLBACK confirms fallback body.

new_defects.title: /sitemap/5.xml still resolves 200 with empty <urlset> — partial close on NEW-2026-04-30-001
new_defects.evidence: Top-level /sitemap.xml index lists chunks 0..4 only. /sitemap/5.xml returns 200 with size 111 bytes, 0 <loc> entries. /sitemap/6.xml returns 404. So the route is no longer crawler-advertised but still resolvable.
new_defects.impact: Low — crawlers won't follow it because it isn't in the index, but the empty 200 response remains a stale code path.
new_defects.recommended_owner: web app (sitemap route) — return 404 for chunks beyond the configured count.

new_defects.title: Confidence mention count drops EXACTLY 2 in /hi vs /en across all 11 working destinations
new_defects.evidence: Per-destination delta computed from grep -c 'confidence' on the rendered HTML: jaipur 11/9, manali 15/13, panaji 10/8, munnar 9/7, varanasi 11/9, darjeeling 9/7, udaipur 9/7, leh 13/11, binsar 8/6, kaza 8/6, shimla 4/10 (Shimla-EN is the broken page so its 4 is the navigation chrome only). Same fixed -2 delta seen on 2026-05-03.
new_defects.impact: Two specific 'confidence' mentions in the EN page body are not being translated to Hindi (likely a static label in a shared component). Cosmetic / copy hygiene issue; does not affect rendering.
new_defects.recommended_owner: web app — find the two un-translated occurrences and route them through the i18n message catalog.
new_defects.reproduction: for slug in jaipur manali panaji munnar varanasi darjeeling udaipur leh binsar kaza; do en=$(curl -s https://www.nakshiq.com/en/destination/$slug | grep -oic confidence); hi=$(curl -s https://www.nakshiq.com/hi/destination/$slug | grep -oic confidence); echo $slug $en $hi $((en-hi)); done — every line ends in '2'.

Did not regression-probe the Hindi /hi/explore page — only English explore was tested, but given the English explore returns 0, it's worth a follow-up.
